rules.title: Global type canonicalization after collection
rules.statement: After item collection, every declared type position is canonicalized by applying the empty substitution (resolving aliases/concrete forms while leaving TypeVar-bearing types unchanged for later mono): struct field types, enum-variant payload types, every fn/generic-fn param and return type, type-alias bodies, module-const types, associated-const-impl types, and associated-type-impl body types.
rules.uncertainty: Concrete behavior of subst_type_sema({}) is inferred from comments (L724-L726): non-generic bodies become concrete; TypeVar-bearing types are left for later substitution.

rules.title: Package name from NAME plus dotted path parts
rules.statement: A module's fully-qualified package name is its NAME, followed by each PATH_PARTS entry's NAME joined with '.' in order (e.g. NAME='c' under parts ['a','b'] => 'a.b.c'-style dotted name). A module with no NAME has the empty package name.

rules.title: Items are always visible within their own package
rules.statement: Access to an item declared in package P from code whose current package is also P is always permitted, regardless of pub/pub(module). Visibility is unchecked when either the defining package or the accessing package context is empty (no scope context).

rules.title: Non-pub items are package-private
rules.statement: An item without `pub` declared in package P is inaccessible from any package other than P; access is an error 'is private to package'.

rules.title: pub(module) has module-linkage visibility
rules.statement: A `pub(module)` item (which also sets is_pub) is visible to other packages only when the accessing code belongs to the SAME owning module-id as the item's defining module; cross-module access is an error 'is module-private'. This module-linkage check precedes the plain is_pub check.

rules.title: Recursive blanket-impl trait satisfaction
rules.statement: A type satisfies trait T if (a) a direct impl T::<concrete> or T::<alt> is registered, or (b) some blanket impl `impl<X> T for X` exists that is unbounded, or whose primary bound trait and all extra bounds are themselves recursively satisfied by the same concrete type. Recursion uses a per-attempt visited set so a failed candidate does not poison sibling candidates; cycles return unsatisfied.

rules.title: Reference-Self impls keyed by mangled $ref_/$mut_ref_ form
rules.statement: `impl T for &C` and `impl T for &mut C` register under mangled keys `T::$ref_<...>` / `T::$mut_ref_<...>`, where a struct pointee uses the bare struct name ($ref_C) and a non-struct pointee uses the full type_str ($ref_&i32). Bound satisfaction for a `&C`/`&mut C` subject must consult both mangled forms.

rules.title: Bound checking is a no-op for non-generic targets
rules.statement: If a target has no type-params, no bound checking is performed on its type-args.

rules.title: Variadic trailing type-param applies to all extra args
rules.statement: If the last type-param is variadic, all type-args at or beyond the non-variadic count are checked against that trailing variadic param; non-variadic params bind positionally.

rules.title: Parametrized bounds checked against substituted type-args
rules.statement: When a bound `I: Iterator<T>` names another of the call's type-params (T) in its type-args, T is replaced by its concrete value from this call (e.g. turbofish T=i32) before bound resolution, rather than deferring the bare TypeVar to monomorphization.

rules.title: Bounds on TypeVar-bearing subjects deferred to mono
rules.statement: A concrete type-arg that still mentions any TypeVar anywhere in its structure (pointee, element, type-args, tuple elems, closure params/ret) is undecidable at collection time and its bound check is deferred to monomorphization. The same deferral applies to AssocType and CfgSlotType subjects, and to Error-kind args (skipped).

rules.title: Sized bound is a no-op marker
rules.statement: `Sized` is a compiler-builtin marker satisfied by every concrete type; a `T: Sized` bound is admitted unconditionally. `?Sized` opt-out is not yet expressible.
rules.divergence: No unsized types yet; ?Sized opt-out not expressible (M7-mt-03).

rules.title: Copy is built-in for bitwise-copyable handle kinds
rules.statement: A `Copy` bound is satisfied without an explicit impl by: a shared reference `&T` (incl. `&dyn Trait`), a raw pointer, a slice `&[T]`, a fn-pointer/fn-value, and a trait-object fat pointer. `&mut T` (exclusive move-only borrow) is NOT Copy and falls through to impl lookup.

rules.title: where &T: Trait satisfied only by reference-Self impl
rules.statement: A `where &T: Trait` (or `&mut T: Trait`) bound on a reference subject is satisfied only by an impl registered for the reference type itself (`T::$ref_<C>` / `T::$mut_ref_<C>`), not by `impl Trait for C`; otherwise it is an error.

rules.title: Auto-trait bounds synthesized from field types
rules.statement: For a bound on an auto trait (e.g. Send/Sync), satisfaction is synthesized structurally from the concrete type's field types; failure reports the offending field (name and type) when known, else 'not inherently <Trait>'.

rules.title: Parametrized bound requires a type-arg-matching impl
rules.statement: For a bound `T: Trait<Args>`, a single-valued Self-name impl hit proves only some Trait impl exists, not one with the right type-args. Satisfaction via name-keyed paths (direct, generic-struct, tuple, alias) requires that SOME registered impl for that Self (enumerated via multi-valued impls_all_, keyed by concrete, unwrapped, and bare struct/enum names) has trait-args equal (after unifying the impl target with the concrete Self) to the bound's substituted type-args. A bound with empty type-args imposes no such constraint. Positions where either side remains abstract are deferred.

rules.title: Bound lifetimes must align with free impl-level lifetime params
rules.statement: When matching a bound's trait-arg lifetimes against an impl's, each non-empty non-'static bound lifetime must align with an impl lifetime that is a free impl-level parameter (not a region concretely pinned at the impl); a 'static bound lifetime is satisfied by an exact 'static match or by a free impl param. Reference pointees and Struct/Enum type-args are walked recursively.

rules.title: Impl-tied lifetime slots require matching bound binders
rules.statement: If an impl uses the same lifetime in two trait-arg positions, the bound must use the same binder in those positions (reverse direction enforced). Bound binders may collapse to one impl lifetime (forward non-injectivity allowed: impl strictly more general). On failure: bound not satisfied (incompatible trait-arg lifetimes).

rules.title: Impl outlives between two skolemized binders is unsatisfiable
rules.statement: If an impl declares a where-clause outlives `'a: 'b` between two impl-side lifetime params that BOTH map to (distinct) bound binders/skolems, the constraint is unsatisfiable under universal quantification and the bound is rejected. Reflexive ('a==' b mapping) is allowed.

rules.title: PartialEq/PartialOrd satisfied by Eq/Ord impls
rules.statement: A `T: PartialEq` bound is accepted via an existing `Eq` impl, and `T: PartialOrd` via an `Ord` impl (on the concrete or unwrapped name).
rules.divergence: SL-sl-02: Logos's Eq currently carries PartialEq's methods; full PartialEq:Eq split pending.

rules.title: Generic-struct impl satisfies bound by base struct name
rules.statement: `impl<T: X> Trait for GenericStruct<T>` registers under the bare base name `Trait::GenericStruct`; a struct/zoned-struct subject satisfies the bound if such a base-name impl exists (and type-args match); the impl's own type-param bounds are validated later at monomorphization.

rules.title: Tuple bound satisfaction by arity with recursive element check
rules.statement: A tuple subject satisfies a bound if a variadic tuple impl `Trait::$tuple$variadic` exists (any arity), or an arity-specific impl `Trait::$tuple$N` exists AND every non-TypeVar element itself satisfies the trait (direct impl, nested tuple arity, or auto-trait). TypeVar elements are deferred to mono.

rules.title: Fn-family bounds satisfied by closures and fn-pointers
rules.statement: An `F: Fn/FnMut/FnOnce(args)->R` bound is satisfied by any closure or fn-value (pointer); arity/arg/ret compatibility is enforced at the call site. A `&F`/`&mut F` whose pointee is a closure, fn-value, or Fn-bounded TypeVar also satisfies the Fn-family bound (autoderef-invoked). A concrete fn-pointer also satisfies a `Trait::$fnptr$N` arity-keyed impl.

rules.title: dyn Trait satisfies its own and supertrait bounds
rules.statement: A `dyn Trait` / unsized-dyn trait-object subject satisfies a `T: Bound` bound when Bound is the object's own trait or any (transitive) supertrait reachable from it.

rules.title: Unsatisfied trait bound is an error
rules.statement:
If none of the satisfaction paths (builtin Copy/Sized, auto, direct impl, blanket, generic-struct, tuple, Fn-family, fnptr, dyn, ref-Self mangling) accept, the bound is unsatisfied: error 'type does not implement trait required by parameter

'.
